questions.question: What should you do if you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Get out and flag down the next vehicle.
Pull to the shoulder, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the shoulder, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the highway shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. Standing or walking on an interstate is dangerous because traffic moves so fast.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, find a safe place to park and rest. Signs of fatigue include struggling to keep your eyes open or drifting from your lane. A short nap is the best solution. Coffee and loud radios cannot replace the rest you need.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One lane is ending. Merge left.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane is ending. Merge left.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign with black markings. It tells you that a lane ahead will end and you need to move to the left lane.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Stop until they are completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: Always stop for blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog. Wait until they are well away from your vehicle before moving. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, which direction should you look?
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again. This helps you see approaching vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer. Also check across the entire intersection to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You can proceed if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road, entrance, or exit. If you see this sign facing you, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: When should you drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum safe speed under perfect conditions. You should drive at the same speed as other traffic, but never faster than the limit. Always adjust your speed for weather, traffic, and road conditions.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and cold showers cannot speed this process.

questions.question: What should you do if you start to feel drowsy while driving?
questions.explanation: When you feel tired, stop at the nearest rest area to take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. These cannot replace sleep and may make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Wear the belt behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together to protect you in a crash. Always wear both your lap and shoulder belts, even with airbags.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: The best way to change lanes is:

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:
questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals, unless an officer is directing traffic instead.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes with speed and distance. It increases your risk of crashing and makes it take longer to make decisions. When tired, you could fall asleep while driving and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or switch drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or switch drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid tired driving, take breaks every hour during a long trip. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas. Do not brake until your vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Proceed because you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any vehicle, cyclist, or pedestrian in the intersection cross first. If a pedestrian begins crossing after the signal flashes, wait until they have crossed before you go.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: When turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe to turn. Slow down to a safe speed for the turn.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. Only go if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Which of these driving skills is affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, make you less alert, and make it hard to focus.

questions.question: You should remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all windows before driving. Clear all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay far away from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase the space between your car and the car in front of you. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black words means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-lane road where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let an aggressive driver pass. Do not try to compete with other drivers. Stay calm and focus on safety.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes always have the right to cross first. You must wait for them.

questions.question: You should adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before moving your car. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seatbelt, and secure any loose items. Do not wait until you are driving to adjust your mirrors.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can reduce your ability to drive safely. They are especially dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Cold showers, black coffee, and exercise do not reduce alcohol in your system. Time is the only way to lower your blood alcohol content. You must wait for your body to process the alcohol.
